# Rami Albatal

> AI for things that matter. Rami Albatal is a data scientist, Head of AI at Beamery, and a researcher in
> lifelogging and AI.

## About

- Leads the AI function at Beamery, a talent lifecycle platform used by large enterprises: AI strategy, research and
  engineering, taking models from prototype to production. Focus areas: talent intelligence, skills, roles and careers.
- Research background in computer vision, information retrieval and personal data. At Dublin City University he worked
  on lifelogging systems and helped organise the NTCIR Lifelog evaluation tasks. Earlier, in Grenoble, he worked on
  automatic image annotation and visual concept detection.

## Selected publications

- Overview of the NTCIR-12 Lifelog Task (NTCIR-12, 2016)
- Advances in Lifelog Data Organisation and Retrieval at the NTCIR-14 Lifelog-3 Task (NTCIR-14, 2019)
- SenseSeer: a mobile-cloud-based lifelogging framework (IEEE ISTAS, 2013)
- Negative FaceBlurring: a privacy-by-design approach to visual lifelogging with Google Glass (2014)
- Visual Phrases for automatic images annotation (CBMI, 2010)

## Personal projects

Live clocks that show the numbers behind the world's big challenges, second by second, against the goals set for them.
Open source under the MIT licence.

- [Emissions Clock](https://ramialbatal.github.io/emissions-clock/): CO2 and methane released by the world and major
  emitters so far this year, with carbon budget and Paris pace checks. [Source](https://github.com/ramialbatal/emissions-clock)
- [Renewables Clock](https://ramialbatal.github.io/renewables-clock/): electricity from solar, wind, hydro and other
  renewables this year, against the goal of tripling capacity by 2030. [Source](https://github.com/ramialbatal/renewables-clock)
- [Jobs Clock](https://ramialbatal.github.io/jobs-clock/): net new jobs this year next to the number of people looking
  for work. [Source](https://github.com/ramialbatal/jobs-clock)
- [clock-core](https://github.com/ramialbatal/clock-core): the shared toolkit behind the clocks.
